headline: High-risk filesystem/MCP pair: Goose can write and share state, while the repo-only prompt-engineering agent offers no isolation or verification boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can read/write the user filesystem and use MCP, so if it ingests content from the prompt-engineering repo or shared files, injected instructions could be treated as trusted. The Awesome-Prompt-Engineering profile is a docs-only repository with no isolation or parser safeguards, so the interaction pathway exists but is indirect.
conditions: IF Goose reads instructions from files in a shared workspace
IF an MCP server or file bridge passes repo content into Goose prompts
mitigations: Keep the repo and Goose in separate directories
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task
Use a read-only mount for the repo
Add a manual review step before Goose consumes file content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose explicitly reads and writes the user filesystem and handles model-provider and extension tokens, while the other agent is a repository of prompt-engineering content with no stated data controls. Shared workspace access creates a plausible leakage path for files in cwd, though the repo itself does not show sensitive data handling.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the same cwd Goose can read
IF Goose extensions or providers receive file contents from that workspace
mitigations: Move sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Run Goose in a separate user account
Unset unused provider and extension tokens
Restrict Goose to a dedicated project directory

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and git-state modification, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. The other agent is non-runnable content, so it does not add write conflict itself, but the shared filesystem state makes concurrent modification conflicts plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Goose instances operate on the same working tree
IF git or file edits occur without external locking
mitigations: Use one Goose instance per working tree
Avoid concurrent git operations
Enable a lockfile or checkout discipline
Stage changes before running another agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: The prompt-engineering repo does not itself act, so it is not a strong upstream authority source for Goose. However, Goose can consume file content and act on tool outputs, so if the repo is used as guidance or input, mistakes could cascade; the lack of a direct action chain keeps this below medium.
conditions: IF Goose is instructed to execute steps copied from the repo
IF Goose treats retrieved text as authoritative without verification
mitigations: Require a human check before execution
Ask Goose to summarize before acting
Limit Goose to read-only analysis mode
Separate research content from operational prompts

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for the prompt-engineering repo, while Goose is a local on-machine agent that handles files and provider tokens. The main compliance concern is local handling of whatever data is placed in the workspace, but the profiles do not show a concrete regulated-data mismatch.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in the workspace Goose can access
IF Goose is configured with a provider or extension subject to stricter retention than the local repo
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Review provider retention settings
Use a local-only model provider
Document which extensions may see workspace files
